items.title: Pro Farmer Estimates 2026 U.S. Corn Crop at 15.344 Billion Bushels, Soybeans at 4.572 Billion
items.author: Farm Journal
items.content:
Kansas City, Mo. (Aug. 21, 2026) — Farm Journal’s today released its highly anticipated national production estimates for the 2026 U.S. corn and soybean crops, estimating corn production at 15.344 billion bushels and soybean production at 4.572 billion bushels.

estimates the 2026 U.S. corn crop at 15.344 billion bushels, based on an average yield of 173.2 bushels per acre.

Given the variables that remain between now and harvest, places the corn crop within a ±1% range of 15.191 billion to 15.498 billion bushels, with a corresponding national yield range of 171.5 to 175.0 bushels per acre.

estimates the 2026 U.S. soybean crop at 4.572 billion bushels, based on an average yield of 53.3 bushels per acre.

Because soybean production remains more sensitive to late-season weather and crop development, places the crop within a ±2% range of 4.481 billion to 4.664 billion bushels, with a corresponding national yield range of 52.2 to 54.4 bushels per acre.

“What we saw throughout the week was a crop with solid potential, but also more variability and fewer bushels than appearances might suggest,” said Chip Flory, host of and western Crop Tour leader. “In corn, lower ear populations, shorter grain length and inconsistent field performance limited upside in a number of areas, while soybeans showed pockets of strong potential but remain more dependent on late-season weather and plant health. Crop Tour helps cut through the headline numbers and show what is actually happening in the field, and this year that firsthand perspective was especially important.”

While Crop Tour provides an important snapshot of fields at a critical point in the growing season, final estimates extend beyond the Tour routes, combining real field data and observations with historical analysis, crop maturity and health, growing conditions, areas not directly sampled and other market intelligence to develop an independent national outlook.

“In a market with more data and forecasting tools than ever, independent, boots-on-the-ground intelligence remains incredibly valuable,” said Bill Watts, Editor. “Crop Tour gives the industry a firsthand view of what’s actually happening in the field and adds important context to the other information producers and markets use to make decisions. That combination is what has made Pro Farmer’s outlook a trusted benchmark year after year.”

For complete Crop Tour results, analysis and continued coverage of the 2026 corn and soybean crops, visit ProFarmer.com.

items.title: Pro Farmer Crop Tour Returns for Its 34th Year, Delivering Agriculture’s Most Trusted Boots-on-the-Ground Crop Insights
items.author: Farm Journal
items.content:
Kansas City, MO., (August 17, 2026) – Today ‘s, Pro Farmerkicks off its 34th annual Crop Tour, continuing a more than three-decade tradition of providing to farms of all sizesan independent, boots-on-the-ground assessment of the nation’s corn and soybean crops.

Each year, scouts who typically spend their days on farms and working in the ag industrytravel thousands of miles across the Corn Belt and volunteer with CropTour. They fan out across seven states to gatherfirsthand field observations that provide producers, agribusinesses and commodity markets with valuable perspective on crop conditions and yield potential. 

Those independent insights have become a trusted benchmark for agriculture, complementing traditional crop reporting, satellite imagery, and remote sensing technologies.

Crop Tour brings together farmers, agronomists, analysts, media and industry leaders for a week of collaboration, conversation and firsthand reporting – an event many call agriculture’s family reunion. Throughout the week, Pro Farmer and Farm Journal deliver real-time updates across digital platforms, social media, newsletters, Farm Journal TV and daily market analysis, helping the agriculture community stay informed as the tour unfolds.

“The Pro Farmer Crop Tour is about far more than just providing another set of crop estimates,” said Bill Watts, Pro Farmer Editor. “It’s about getting the first, comprehensive, boots-on-the-ground look at what’s actually going on across the most important corn-and-soybean growing areas. And that ground truth gives farmers and everyone involved in agriculture a real-time read on what’s happening in the field and what it means for the market.”As part of Farm Journal’s ongoing commitment to serving American agriculture, live coverage of Crop Tour will be available Monday through Thursday from 8 AM CT to 3 PM CT on , ,  and Farm Journal’s YouTube Channel. Daily results will be released each night during a live simulcast that begins at 7:55 PM CT on these same outlets. Extensive coverage will also be shared across social media, search for #PFTour26 to follow along.
